summary: With the fixups.json sentinel strip in place the original now compiles and renders for the first time, and both sides are recognizably the same thing — a multi-mode, 2 Hz-beat-locked sound sequencer with the same look vocabulary (row bars, VU-style ramps, dot lattices, per-pixel gradient fields) and the same single inert slider — but the macro schedule is wrong (original alternates a 181 s FULLY BLACK phase with a ~212 s active phase, 56% dark at 20 fps; port never goes dark at 20 fps, 4.9%), the mode sequences never align at any lag, the port owns an ~8 s-per-cycle mode that blanks on every other rendered frame (a frame-coupled 10 Hz strobe at 20 fps, 20 Hz at 40 fps) that the original never produces, and the port freezes solid when the sensor feed is removed while the original keeps animating.
observations: RE-JUDGE STATUS: the original now RENDERS. meta.json warnings/provenance.fixups record `stripLinesMatching` removing 2 lines (`BY_REMOVING_THESE_INVALID_LINES_I_PROMISE_THIS_IS_RUNNING_ON_A_PIXELBLAZE_V3`, `I_UNDERSTAND_THIS_PATTERN_CAN_BRICK_A_PIXELBLAZE_VERSION_2`); sides.orig.compileError is null on every run. The prior orig-unrenderable subtype-(b) verdict is superseded. epeSha256 1de5be146bf8, portSha256 e63ea541360e, harnessSha256 bfd91d43d7f9.

CONTROL SURFACE MATCHES EXACTLY: both sides expose one control, name `sliderChooseManualPattern`, kind `slider`, label `ChooseManualPattern`. Both sides report wantsSensors true and are fed `beat120` under `--sensors auto`.

MACRO SCHEDULE — the headline divergence. Measured over 1400 s at four frame rates (labels rj-span5 / rj-longspan / rj-span20 / rj-span40), taking 'quiet' = meanBrightness <= 1 for >= 15 s. ORIGINAL: quiet phases of 180-181 s at EVERY fps (5, 10, 20, 40 — perfectly time-based), separated by active phases of 137/136/212/205 s at 5/10/20/40 fps; fully-black frame fraction 0.671 / 0.665 / 0.562 / 0.555. PORT: quiet phases of exactly 64 s at 5 and 10 fps, and NO quiet phase at all at 20 or 40 fps; active phases 135 s at 5/10 fps; black frame fraction 0.113 / 0.073 / 0.049 / 0.047. At the harness default rig and fps the original spends 181 s of every ~394 s cycle at literally zero on all 256 pixels; the port runs continuously.

The original's opening 180.4 s are entirely black — this is a real property, not a warm-up artefact of one setting. Onset measured at t = 180.35-180.67 s at fps 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 40 (frame indices 542, 903, 1083, 1443, 1805, 2708, 3611, 4513, 7221 — all the same wall-clock second), and unchanged by --seed 7, --seed 1234, --wall-clock 1756000175, --wall-clock 1700000000, --sensors off, and every slider value 0..1. Only fps 2 and fps 4 report an early onset (15.5 s / 11.5 s); those two rates sample the 2 Hz beat120 feed beat-synchronously and are the low-fps aliasing artefact JUDGE.md warns about — ignore them. Onset is not a step: brightness ramps 1,2,2 -> 5 -> 10 -> 22 in 10-frame (0.5 s = one beat) increments.

The original's cycle is ~318 s at 5-10 fps and ~394 s at 20-40 fps, with a super-period of ~636 s (two DIFFERENT active sequences alternate: the 5 s-binned brightness profile of the 180-320 s active phase repeats at 830-970 s, not at 496-636 s). The port's cycle is a single repeated sequence at 198.7 s (autocorrelation of meanBrightness over 1200 s at 10 fps: lag 1987 frames r=0.77, harmonics at 397.4 s r=0.62 and 596.1 s r=0.47) and ~111 s at 20-40 fps. No fps makes the two cycle lengths agree.

The two sides' mode sequences do not correspond at any time offset. Cross-correlating 1 s-binned (meanR,meanG,meanB) vectors over 1200 s with a lag scan of +/-400 s gives a best correlation of only 0.097 (at -352 s); at lag 0 it is 0.010. They are not a shifted version of each other.

PORT-ONLY DEFECT — every-other-frame blanking. In one mode the port alternates a lit frame with a pixel-exact BLACK frame. Example at t=209-213 s, 20 fps (rj-alive): port meanBrightness reads 34,0,57,0,55,0,50,0,43,0,35,0,63,0,... while the original over the same frames reads a smooth beat envelope 2,2,...,24,11,7,7,7,7,7,8,25,24,7,... with no zeros. The alternation is per-FRAME, not per-time: at 40 fps the port still alternates every frame (35,0,67,0,66,0,...) = a 20 Hz strobe, at 20 fps a 10 Hz strobe, at 5 fps 2.5 Hz. Census over 1400 s: port isolated-zero frames 175 (5 fps) / 295 (10 fps) / 959 (20 fps), longest alternating run 20 / 40 / 80 isolated zeros = ~8 s of strobing per cycle at every rate. Original: 20 / 33 / 57 isolated zeros total (0.2-0.3% of frames) and a longest run of 1-2 — i.e. never. The strobe is plainly visible as dense fine horizontal striping in port-rhythm.png of rj-sens-on (205-235 s) and as alternate black cells in port-motion.png of rj-alive.

SENSOR-OFF DEGRADATION DIFFERS. Same window (205-235 s, 20 fps), --sensors off: ORIGINAL keeps animating — meanBrightness {avg 22.5, min 10, max 72}, motion {avg 3.5, max 89}, zeroMotionFrames 0/600, trend steady. PORT is completely FROZEN — meanBrightness exactly 7 on all 600 frames (min=max=first=last=7), motion and motionLit 0 on every frame, zeroMotionFrames 600/600. The port has no self-running content whatsoever; the original does.

BEAT LOCK IS RIGHT ON BOTH SIDES. Autocorrelation of the raw motion series over the 180-320 s active window at 20 fps: original has a local peak at lag 10 frames = 0.500 s (r=0.579, against 0.45 at lags 8-9 and 11-12); port peaks at lag 5 frames = 0.250 s (r=0.753) and lag 10 = 0.500 s (r=0.735). Both are locked to the 2 Hz beat120 feed; the port additionally carries a strong half-beat (4 Hz) component the original does not emphasise.

LOOK VOCABULARY OVERLAPS WELL. --dump analysis of 16x16 frames across the shared 180-320 s active window shows both sides drawing from the same set of structures: row-uniform horizontal bars (orig at 235.25 s: 12/16 rows uniform; port at 235.25 s: 16/16 uniform, 2 colours, exactly 134-brightness bars in rows 2-5 and 8-11), monotone VU-style level ramps (port at 270.25 s: rows 0,0,1,1,3,3,9,9,18,18,36,36,73,73,0,0 — a doubling ramp; orig shows the equivalent at 305.25 s with rows ...,1,1,95,107,...), sparse dot lattices (orig 185.15 s, 4 colours, 66% lit, regular 2-px column comb 21,2,21,2,21,2...; port 185.15 s, 70 colours, 34% lit), and dense per-pixel gradient fields (orig 220.15 s: 213 distinct colours, 100% lit; orig 250.4 s: 210 colours, 96% lit; port 250.4 s: 159 colours, 86% lit).

BUT AT MATCHED TIMES THE MODES DISAGREE. rj-alive contact sheets (skip 180, 60 s, 20 fps): at 180.0 s orig black / port magenta dot field; 190.9 s orig dim dots / port red bars; 196.3 s orig sparse blue dots / port solid green upper half; 212.7 s orig red bars / port green bars; 218.2 s orig red-white-grey bars / port black with one white dot; 234.5 s orig black / port purple bar. Dumps confirm: at 270.25 s the original is 1 colour, 0% lit, all-black while the port draws an 88%-lit 8-level ramp; at 220.15 s the original is a 213-colour full field while the port is 2 colours and 0.7 mean brightness.

PORT IS DIMMER IN ITS ACTIVE PHASES. Mean brightness restricted to frames with brightness > 1, over 1400 s: original 37.2 / 35.5 / 29.0 / 28.2 at 5/10/20/40 fps; port 21.2 / 20.7 / 21.7 / 22.2. That is a 25-40% deficit at every rate.

SEGMENT STRUCTURE IS SIMILAR IN SHAPE. Segmenting the shared 180-320 s active window on normalized-RGB jumps, both sides play a handful of long (8-30 s) single-look segments and then a burst of rapid 1-2 s colour changes: original rapid burst at 258-274 s (green -> teal -> blue -> violet -> magenta -> orange, one second each), port rapid burst at 256-273 s (green -> teal -> blue -> magenta). So the sequencer's own section structure is reproduced in kind, just not in content or phase.

BOTH SIDES ARE ONLY MILDLY STOCHASTIC AND THE ORIGINAL'S SCHEDULE IS SEED-INDEPENDENT. Over 260 s at 20 fps, meanBrightness mean-abs-diff vs seed 1: orig 0.158 (seed 7) / 0.187 (seed 1234); port 2.950 / 2.860. The original's quiet/active block boundaries are identical across seeds, so its 181 s dark phase is deterministic schedule, not an RNG draw.

RIG BEHAVIOUR. At skip 205 s the original's mean brightness is 37 on strip/60 px, 37 on grid 8x8 (64 px) and 37 on grid 16x16 (256 px) — pixel-count-independent in that mode; the port reads 29 / 27 / 26 on the same three rigs. On --grid 48x48 (2304 px) the ORIGINAL hits a harness engine limit — `RUNTIME ERR @-1: array element budget exceeded (arrays are never freed)` — and renders black, while the port renders normally (mean 27). That is an engine/rig ceiling on the original, not a port fidelity finding, but it means large-grid comparisons are unavailable for this pair.

CAVEAT ON CAUSE: from rendered output alone I cannot tell whether the original's 181 s fully-black phase is authored behaviour (a deliberate silent section) or a gap in our engine that silences part of its mode list. It is exactly time-based (181 s at every fps from 3 to 40) and survives seed, wall-clock, sensor and dial changes, which reads more like pattern logic than an engine fault, but the firewall forbids checking. The other divergences (frame-blanking strobe, frozen-without-sensors, non-aligning mode sequence, 25-40% brightness deficit) stand on their own regardless.

dials.name: sliderChooseManualPattern
dials.origEffect: INERT. --probe-controls: maxDelta 0.00 / maxDeltaLit 0.00 at 0, 0.5, 1. Manual sweep at 0, 0.1, 0.2, ..., 1.0 over a 320 s window at 10 fps (spanning the full 181 s dark phase plus a whole 137 s active phase) gave identical stats at every value: dark fraction 0.630 and mean brightness 14.4 for all eleven settings. --dump byte-comparison of three frames at 208.15 / 214.25 / 222.4 s (inside the active phase) at values 0, 0.5 and 1 vs untouched: BYTE-IDENTICAL in all cases. Dial effect unverifiable from output.
dials.portEffect: INERT, identically. Same probe (0.00 / 0.00), same 11-value 320 s sweep (dark fraction 0.087, mean 12.9 at every value), same three-frame dump byte-identical to untouched at 0, 0.5 and 1. Note the setter-interaction workaround does not apply: this is the only control either side exposes, so there is no second control to pin.

feedback: PORT BUG 1 (most concrete, fix first): the port has a mode — roughly 8 s long, once per ~199 s cycle, seen around t=205-220 s at 20 fps as green horizontal bars — that renders a completely BLACK frame on every other rendered frame. meanBrightness there reads 34,0,57,0,55,0,50,0,... at 20 fps and 35,0,67,0,66,0,... at 40 fps, i.e. the blanking is tied to the frame counter, not to time, so it strobes at fps/2 Hz (2.5 Hz at 5 fps up to 20 Hz at 40 fps). The original never emits an isolated black frame in this way (57 in 28,000 frames, longest run 1). Whatever advances that mode is clearing the frame and only painting on alternate ticks; the intended look is a steady bar field with a beat envelope on top.

PORT BUG 2: with the sensor feed removed (--sensors off) the port locks to a single static frame — meanBrightness exactly 7 and motion exactly 0 on all 600 frames of a 30 s window — while the original keeps moving (motion avg 3.5, brightness swinging 10 to 72, zeroMotionFrames 0). The port has no non-audio drive at all. The original clearly runs its sequencer off a time base as well as off audio; add the free-running component so the pattern still animates on a board with no sensor expansion.

PORT BUG 3 (macro schedule): the original alternates a phase in which the whole rig is exactly black for 181 s with an active phase of 137 s (at 5-10 fps) or ~212 s (at 20-40 fps); the port's quiet phase is only 64 s at 5-10 fps and DISAPPEARS ENTIRELY at 20 and 40 fps, where the port never stops. The original's dark phase is exactly 181 s at every frame rate tested (3 through 40 fps) — a clean time-based timer — so the port should have a matching fps-invariant silent/quiet section of that length. Right now a viewer watching for ten minutes sees the original dark 56% of the time and the port dark 5% of the time.

PORT BUG 4 (fps coupling of the cycle): the port's cycle length changes between 10 fps (198.7 s) and 20 fps (111 s), and its quiet phase vanishes above 10 fps. The original's quiet phase is rock-solid fps-invariant, though its active phase also lengthens between 10 and 20 fps (136 s -> 212 s), so some frame-count dependence exists on both sides. Aim for the original's split: an exactly time-based 181 s quiet timer, with whatever advances the active sequence being the only frame-sensitive part.

PORT BUG 5 (brightness): during active phases the port averages 21-22 mean brightness against the original's 28-37, at every frame rate. Roughly a 25-40% shortfall; check the per-mode output levels rather than a global scale, since the port matches the original's peak values in some modes (port hits 116 vs original 111 in the 205-235 s window) but sits far below in others.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT AND MUST BE PRESERVED: (a) the control surface is exact — one slider named sliderChooseManualPattern, label ChooseManualPattern, and it is inert on BOTH sides (byte-identical dumps at 0/0.5/1 over a 320 s window), so the port is NOT at fault for the dead dial and should not be 'fixed' to make it live; (b) the 2 Hz beat lock is correct (motion autocorrelation peaks at lag 10 frames at 20 fps on both sides); (c) the look vocabulary is right — row-uniform bar fields, monotone level ramps, sparse dot lattices, dense per-pixel gradient fields all appear on both sides with comparable lit fractions and colour counts; (d) the section structure is right in kind — both sides play several 8-30 s single-look segments and then a rapid 1-2 s-per-colour burst.

PROCEDURE NOTE FOR THE NEXT JUDGE OR FIXER: never survey this pair at 2 or 4 fps. Those rates sample the 2 Hz beat120 feed beat-synchronously and make the original appear to wake at 11-15 s instead of its true 180.4 s. Use >= 5 fps for schedule work and 20 fps for rhythm. Also budget at least 1400 s of simulated time per run: the original's super-period is ~636 s (it alternates two different active sequences), so a 300 s survey shows only half of its content. Runs are cheap — 1400 s at 40 fps completes in seconds.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE FIXER (needs code, which the judge may not read): is the original's 181 s all-black phase authored, or is it our engine silencing part of its mode list? It is deterministic, seed-independent, wall-clock-independent, dial-independent and exactly time-based at every fps from 3 to 40, which argues for authored. If it turns out to be an engine gap, ignore feedback item 3 and re-score; the other four defects are independent of it.
